teams.heading: Fiji score 314 points and concede 351 over last 11 tests
teams.body: The senior men's national side averaged 28.5 points scored and 31.9 points conceded per game across their last 11 fixtures. During this window, the Flying Fijians accumulated a total of 314 points while shipping 351 to their opponents. The team's biggest win in this period came in September 2025, when Fiji defeated Canada 63-10 on home soil during the Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage.

teams.heading: Will Joseph stakes England claim as Gloucester thrash Harlequins in Premiership rout
teams.body: Gloucester centre Will Joseph bolstered his chances for an England recall during Saturday’s emphatic 48-0 victory over Harlequins. Joseph was the pick of the backline in an eight-try demolition at Kingsholm, scoring once and repeatedly breaking the line to pressure the Harlequins defence. With Steve Borthwick finalising his squad for the upcoming Test against Australia, Joseph’s physical performance suggests he is ready for further caps. Meanwhile, Northampton’s George Hendy impressed at full-back, though regular international Tommy Freeman struggled in the same role.

lead.why: Will Joseph’s dominant performance in Gloucester's 48-0 win over Harlequins puts him firmly back in Steve Borthwick's selection thoughts for the November Tests.

teams.heading: France face Fiji having won their last meeting 34-21 in November 2025
teams.body: France's senior men's side occupy third place in the Nations Championship table following their 42-15 victory against Japan in Round 3. Fabien Galthié's side have recorded two wins and one defeat across their opening three fixtures, scoring 116 points while conceding 75 in the tournament so far. Les Bleus next face Fiji in Round 4, a side they defeated 34-21 during an international friendly at home in November 2025. This remains the only recent result between the two teams as the competition resumes.

teams.heading: Ireland women seal seven-try victory over Japan in Cork test
teams.body: The Ireland women's side secured a comprehensive 43-19 win over Japan at Virgin Media Park on Saturday. Despite conceding an early try, the hosts dominated the remainder of the match, crossing the whitewash four times before half-time. Beibhinn Parsons extended her record of total Ireland tries to 25 during the second period, while debuts for Sophie Barrett and Alana McInerney were marked by tries off the bench. The team now turns its attention to an upcoming series against South Africa.

teams.heading: Bath monitor Edinburgh scrum-half Hector Patterson amid international allegiance switch
teams.body: Bath are monitoring Edinburgh scrum-half Hector Patterson as the 21-year-old approaches the end of his current contract. While Patterson has represented Scotland at age-grade level—including winning the 2024 World Rugby U20 Trophy—he remains eligible to play for England through a grandparent. With his contract expiring at the end of this season, his potential move to the Premiership could complicate his international future, as he has yet to be tied to Scotland at the senior international level.

lead.why: The interest from Bath in Hector Patterson represents a tangible recruitment development regarding a Scottish-eligible player.

teams.heading: Josh Adams eyes third World Cup as fitness return nears
teams.body: Wales wing Josh Adams has confirmed he is targeting a third Rugby World Cup appearance as he nears a return to action. The 31-year-old missed the international defeat to South Africa in July with a calf injury and has been sidelined for Cardiff’s opening fixtures. Adams is now back in training and expects to be available for international duty in November, as the squad prepares for the upcoming Nations Championship tests against Japan, New Zealand, and Australia.

Following changes to the starting lineup, Hunter Reich moves into the pack while Taj Scarr earns a start on the wing. The match serves as the conclusion to the series, with the Australian Schoolboys also playing the New Zealand Māori.

teams.heading: Japan women suffer seven-try defeat against Ireland in Cork test
teams.body: The Japan women's side concluded their tour with a 43-19 defeat against Ireland at Virgin Media Park on Saturday. Despite an early try from Sakurako Korai and further scores from Nami Asari and Nijiho Nagata, the visitors were unable to contain an expansive Irish attack. The match followed a competitive outing in Galway the previous weekend, marking the end of a demanding two-match series for the Sakura XV in the northern hemisphere.

teams.heading: Ardie Savea confirms move to the Blues for 2027 season
teams.body: All Blacks captain Ardie Savea has officially signed with the Blues for the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific season. The 32-year-old, who previously played for Moana Pasifika in 2025, confirmed his return to New Zealand following his latest sabbatical with the Kobe Steelers. Savea stated that the Auckland-based club has always been close to his heart, with Blues chief executive Karl Budge noting the move is central to the club’s ambition to reconnect with the city and bolster their leadership ranks.

teams.heading: André Esterhuizen and Edwill van der Merwe star as Sharks defeat Leinster
teams.body: Returning Springboks spearheaded the Sharks to a 26-20 bonus-point victory over Leinster at Kings Park on Saturday to preserve their unbeaten start in the United Rugby Championship. Recalled by coach JP Pietersen alongside fellow internationals, captain André Esterhuizen and winger Edwill van der Merwe both crossed the tryline in the second half. Manu Tshituka and Lili Bester also scored as the hosts overcame a slow start, with Eben Etzebeth, Ox Nche, and Ethan Hooker making strong impacts off the bench.
